content: The South African patient monitoring system includes a comprehensive Patient Details Folder that captures essential demographic and medical information. This folder records the patient’s phone number, sex (male or female), and a detailed history of pregnancies, including the year, gestational age, delivery details, sex of the baby, birth weight, and outcomes. Social history and support systems are also documented, alongside risk factors such as family history of heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, or mental illness. Lifestyle factors like smoking (including the year started, quantity per day, and cessation details), alcohol consumption (type, weekly quantity, and cessation details), and physical inactivity are noted. Other risk factors include sexual abuse, substance abuse, and family history of cholesterol issues or mental illness. A Chronic Problem List is maintained, detailing the year or date of diagnosis, associated conditions, and relevant notes. Chronic conditions tracked include hypertension, ischemic heart disease, cardiac failure, diabetes, cerebrovascular accidents (CVA), transient ischemic attacks (TIA), asthma, peripheral artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), retinopathy, epilepsy, chronic renal disease, depression, generalized anxiety disorder, psychosis, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and substance-induced disorders. HIV-related information, such as prior antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimens, baseline CD4 counts, and treatment outcomes, is also recorded. Tuberculosis (TB) outcomes, including drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) and extrapulmonary TB (EPTB), are documented alongside other chronic conditions. The folder includes a section for past medical history, allergies, and side effects, which are highlighted in red. Blood group and treatment dates are also recorded. Adult stationery includes the patient’s ID number, first and last name, address, date of birth, and next of kin details. This section serves as an ongoing summary of the patient’s health, ensuring that any clinician reviewing the file in the future can understand the major features of the patient’s clinical course. The system also incorporates consolidated guidelines for person-centered HIV patient monitoring and case surveillance. HIV and TB statuses are monitored, including ART regimens, CD4 counts, viral loads, and TB screening or treatment (e.g., IPT, DS-TB, DR-TB). Laboratory investigations such as creatinine, eGFR, RPR, Hb, ALT, cholesterol, triglycerides, and HbA1c are routinely performed. Urinalysis, pregnancy tests, and glucose levels are also assessed. Reproductive health is addressed through screenings for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), family planning (FP), male medical circumcision (MMC), and cervical cancer (PAP smears). Pregnancy monitoring includes last menstrual period (LMP), symphysis-fundal height (SFH), gestational age (GA), and ultrasound findings. Mental health evaluations focus on mood, substance abuse, and psychosocial risks, while lifestyle factors such as smoking, diet, exercise, and drug use are reviewed. Referrals, follow-up appointments, and test results are tracked, with healthcare providers and data capturers signing off on each entry. This structured approach facilitates comprehensive patient care and continuity across healthcare providers.
